headline: Team calendars can only be shared inside the organisation today, so a team working with outside guests sends free/busy by hand, and nothing says who has seen what once it has left.
summary: Sharing stops at the organisation's edge, because guests have no identity the permission service can check. Two teams already export free/busy to outside tools by hand, and support has asked who viewed a shared calendar. Success is a guest who sees a team's free time with no account and no export. Who this is for: Nadia, a team lead who books outside partners, and Tom, a guest who only needs to know when to call. A design brief with screens is recommended: one dialog and one guest page.

recommends.reason: One dialog and one guest page, with no development run to follow at once.

decisions.decision: Guests get a signed link, never an account of their own
decisions.rationale: The invite flow already signs links. Accounts would need a second identity store.

decisions.decision: Free/busy is what a guest sees; event details stay out of this design
A share can be revoked by the calendar owner and by an organisation admin
The persona cards draw on the support team's own descriptions of who asks for this
Offline access on the phone stays out of scope for now

risks.risk: Drafted story: a team lead shares a whole team calendar with one guest link, which assumes a grant the permission service has no row for today and may need a new kind of grant
risks.change: scope the story to single-member calendars

risks.risk: Drafted story: a guest removed from a project stops seeing its schedule at once, while the mobile client keeps a week of calendars and may show it until the next sync runs
risks.change: say a revoke is enforced on the next sync
